items.reason: Both cross-card hops are genuinely reliable. Hop (a) Exquisite Blood emit:life:gain (Controller=You) -> Vito trigger:life:gain (Controller=You): You subset You, ControllerSubsumes(You,You)=Yes. Hop (b) Vito emit:life:loss:opponent (now Kind:Opponent -> Subject Controller=Opponent, NOT runtime-chosen Target) -> Exquisite Blood trigger:life:loss (Controller=Opponent): ControllerSubsumes(Opponent,Opponent)=Yes. No scope leak: post-sharpen recipient is the CR-pinned 'opponent' category (CR 102.2/102.3, glossary 'Opponent' = someone a player is playing against), provably disjoint from 'you' (CR 109.4; operator encodes You perp Opponent Disjoint). The pre-sharpen Kind:Target referent was runtime-chosen -> Unknown -> AMBER; the sharpen replaced it with a category the CR decides, so AMBER->GREEN is earned honestly, not a false positive. A singular targeted opponent losing life is a member of the existential set 'an opponent loses life', so every emitted object satisfies the consumer universally. Cycle steady-state (CoCostsSatisfied/Balanced) is a one-time-seed Firable property, orthogonal to per-edge reliability.

Structurally identical to Exquisite Blood + Vito. Bloodthirsty Conqueror's trigger filter is Controller=Opponent and its gainLife effect targets Player:You, mirroring Exquisite Blood exactly (verified in AST and single-card snapshot). The life-loss hop closes on ControllerSubsumes(Opponent,Opponent)=Yes and the life-gain hop on You subset You. Same CR basis (102.2/102.3, 109.4, glossary 'Opponent'); same honest AMBER->GREEN earned by the Vito parse sharpen. No false positive.

cr_basis: CR 102.2 — In a two-player game, a player's opponent is the other player.
CR 102.3 — In a multiplayer game between teams, a player's opponents are all players not on their team.
Glossary Opponent — Someone a player is playing against (rules 102.2, 102.3).
CR 109.4 — controller identity (operator: You perp Opponent => Disjoint).
